chapter: Trumpet styles and early New Orleans scene
title: Buddy Petit's style and Joe Oliver
summary: Punch says Petit's style was hard to imitate, and that he first saw King Oliver in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I see. Well who did Buddy Petit play like? Anybody today or any other record jammer?

Well I've been trying to figure that out. Buddy Petit had a style, just was hard to get into, you know. I can blow a lot like him, but I just can't keep his style up going, cause he could go way down and get them pedal notes, you know, bring one of them, diminished chords and things and all like that. He could play a real good horn.
Was Joe Oliver doing anything like him at all?

Well, I believe he got something out of it from Joe Oliver. That's a fellow I never did know could do, Joe Oliver. And the first time I seen him was when I went to Chicago. I didn't never see him down here. First time I saw him. I went to Chicago to the plantation one night, the whole show went out and I went with him. And that's the first time I seen King Oliver.
